## Standard

<a id="Yaml"></a>

### YAML

`Yaml` · `src/yaml.ts:27`

The marks of a YAML document in the block style: what ends a key, opens an entry of a sequence, opens a literal block, opens a comment, ends a line.

Source: YAML Ain't Markup Language, version 1.2.2 (2021): § 5.4 line breaks, § 6.6 comments, § 8.1.2 literal style, § 8.2.1 block sequences, § 8.2.2 block mappings · `https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `colon` | `:` | Ends the key of an entry of a mapping (§ 8.2.2) |
| `space` | `" "` | Separates a key's colon, a sequence's dash or a comment's mark from what follows |
| `dash` | `-` | Opens an entry of a block sequence (§ 8.2.1) |
| `literal` | `\|` | Opens a literal block: the lines under it, deeper, are kept as they are (§ 8.1.2) |
| `comment` | `#` | Opens a comment, to the end of the line (§ 6.6) |
| `endOfLine` | `"\n"` | Ends a line: a line feed (§ 5.4) |

## Syntax element

<a id="YamlDocument"></a>

### A YAML document

`YamlDocument` · `src/yaml.ts:49` · status: **held**

The comment lines that head it, then its nodes in the block style: a key and its text on one line, a key alone over what it holds, one level deeper; an entry of a sequence after a dash, a mapping in it starting on the dash's line; lines kept as they are in a literal block. A text is written as it is when YAML reads it back the same, otherwise in double quotes, as JSON writes a string (YAML 1.2 reads JSON's strings).

Section: § 8.2 Block collection styles; § 7.3.1 Double-quoted style · `https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#82-block-collection-styles`

| Mark | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `indent` | `"  "` | One level deeper: two spaces, as wide as a dash and its space, as GitHub's examples write it |
| `top` | `""` | No indentation: the keys of the document itself |
| `plain` | `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/@ -]*[A-Za-z0-9._/@-]$\|^[A-Za-z0-9]$` | A text written without quotes: letters, digits, and marks that mean nothing to YAML inside a text, without a space at its end |
